beyond_this_part.finding: the reading gloss in the story bible at p21 calls the bamboo wife 'the jointed rattan bolster leaned on in summer heat', while the translator's note at p11, marked 'as in the bible', describes it as 'a hollow bolster of woven bamboo leaned upon in summer heat'; the two formulations for the same object do not match, so the bible should be checked and put right.
beyond_this_part.why: the Japanese in both places is the same word, 竹婦人《ちくふじん》 in p11 and 竹婦人 in p21, and the house brief says the passage in front of the desk beats the bible rather than quietly working around a discrepancy

declined.reason: "with gathering speed" does render the brisk, uninterrupted pace of Liu's fortune tilting "in quick, steady rhythm"; the note's "declined steadily" would strip the ton-ton-byōshi tempo from the decline report, and the suggested phrasing is stet.

would replace "willingly brought about the loss" with "willingly threw away", which hardens Liu's passive, chance-caused loss of his fortune into a deliberate act of throwing; the Japanese "by chancing to meet... he willingly came to lose this heaven-given fortune" keeps the odd pairing, and "by chancing" is acceptable English for it.

disagreements.choice: Restored the token beard (F1's wording): "grew on the tip of his chin, as a mere token, a beard like a rat's tail".
disagreements.faithful_side: F1: 申訳だけに means a merely token beard, not a beard grown by way of apology.
disagreements.readable_side: R3: "by way of apology" suggests he is apologising, when the point is a token, scanty beard.

data.say: Changes made: p2 spelled out "likely to steam" (R1); p4 the monk now waves rather than flourishes the fly-whisk (R2) and squats "with pompous self-importance, like a turkey" (F3); p5 the beard is "as a mere token" (F1/R3) and the robe is a "black-cloth gown" (F2); p10 the drinking is "a capacity beyond ordinary men" (R4); p12 Liu heaves up his "fat body, hot-looking in itself" (R5); p13 the rumours are "going round in full force" (R6); p17 the eyes are "like faceted amethyst" (R7); p40 Liu "was the first to bow his head" (R8); p41 the monk is "telling him not to move" (R9); p42 ordinary men "go through schooling and the like" (R10); p45 the skin "had not an ounce of elasticity to answer them" (R11). On F4 I checked the Japanese: 芬々たる酒香 is richly fragrant, and "thick reek" does make it foul and settle a tone the text leaves split, so the note is right in substance; however my edit to that sentence misfired and left the wording "effect" in place of the noun phrase, so the sentence at p46 as it stands is broken and must be restored to "a rich fragrant smell of wine assailed Liu's nose without pause" before this part can leave the desk — I have not been able to re-apply that correction, and the sentence should not be published as it now reads. The remaining readable notes I weighed but left stet for the reasons given under Declined. House log: All notes checked against the Japanese; the token beard and the black cloth were restored, translationese was cleared where it did not touch the reading, and the one broken sentence at p46 is flagged for repair rather than passed on silently.
